title: How close does greedy get?
hook: The achieved score and its lower bound are different.

knows: A score to maximise over many candidates; distance between points.
doesNotKnow: greedy can be suboptimal yet have a qualified lower bound. Neither “greedy always fails” nor “diminishing returns makes greedy exact” is correct.

misconception: greedy can be suboptimal yet have a qualified lower bound. Neither “greedy always fails” nor “diminishing returns makes greedy exact” is correct.
objective: greedy can be suboptimal yet have a qualified lower bound. Neither “greedy always fails” nor “diminishing returns makes greedy exact” is correct.

claims.text: Exact marginal greedy recomputes gains and breaks ties by stable alphabetic ID; exhaustive enumeration checks every subset of size<=2. Basecoverage picks A+B for5, optimalB+C for6; achieved5/6 differs from finite-k lower bound3/4. New coverage achieves6/8. Complement f(BC)=100, f(S)=1 if A present without BC,else0 is normalized/monotone but not submodular and gives greedy1,opt100. Dashed score line is a theorem bound only in valid coverage modes.

claims.text: Title: How close does greedy get? Hook: The achieved score and its lower bound are different. Choose two sets: A={1,2,3,4}, B={1,2,5}, C={3,4,6}. Can exact marginal greedy miss the best pair? Options: Yes / No; answer 0.

claims.text: The retained greedy pair covers 5 while the best pair covers 6. For normalized, nonnegative, monotone submodular functions with a cardinality limit and exact marginal greedy, the finite two-pick bound is three quarters of optimum, at least 1 minus 1/e. The achieved ratio is five sixths. Complementarity removes the assumption and the guarantee.
claims.source: Local model.ts and model.repro.mjs; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01588971 (original publisher abstract, nondecreasing normalized finite-k greedy bound 1-((k-1)/k)^k; full proof not reproduced), opened2026-10-19 for method context, not verification of toy outputs.
claims.address: Demo.tsx reveal and retained original-case witness

claims.text: A valid normalized monotone submodular coverage task allows two picks and has optimum 8. What does the finite two-pick bound ensure? For two picks, 1-(1-1/2)^2 is 3/4. Three quarters of 8 is 6; the achieved result may be higher.

claims.text: The guarantee requires normalization, nonnegative monotonicity, submodularity, cardinality constraint and exact marginal choices. Not arbitrary costs/noisy gains/nonmonotone objectives; source theorem is not independently verified by testing these examples.
